newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were seen opening slightly higher Wednesday, despite further strength in the U.S. dollar overnight, with pent up demand in the platinum group metals (PGMs) market lifting palladium to its highest fix in London since June 12.
COMEX December gold was seen opening unchanged to up 50 cents an ounce from Tuesday's close at $329.80, after trading a $329.70-330.90 range in overnight ACCESS trade.
In the bullion market spot gold, was quoted $326.75/25 early, compared with the London Wednesday morning fix at $326.40 and the New York close Tuesday at $325.70/30.

The U.S. dollar reached a new 47 month high against the Swiss franc overnight, after hitting a new six year high against the mark early this week and a new seven year high on dollar's trade weighted index.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks fell just 32 ounces Tuesday to 919,728 ounces, while COMEX silver stocks fell 1,236,805 ounces to 171,829,556 ounces.
COMEX September silver was seen opening unchanged to up 0.5 cent an ounce from Tuesday's close at $4.325.
PGM futures surged even higher on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) overnight, as shortcovering continued, leaving the active TOCOM April 1998 palladium contract limit up at a new contract high.

Russian exports of PGMs have resumed, under the annual supply contract to Japan, and in the spot market, but next deliveries are not expected to arrive until early August and volumes are not meeting demand.

NYMEX October platinum was seen opening unchanged to up $1.00 an ounce from Tuesday's close at $421.10 and NYMEX September palladium was seen unchanged to up $1.00 also from the previous close at $194.90, after the contract hit a new contract high on Tuesday.
